title: List encoding and decoding
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $f$ be a decoder from Boolean lists to either no result or an element of $\alpha$ together with a remaining Boolean list, and let $g$ assign a Boolean list to each element of $\alpha$. For a finite list $A$ in $\alpha$, suppose that for every $a\in A$ and every Boolean-list suffix $r$, decoding the concatenation of $g(a)$ with $r$ returns $(a,r)$. Then for every natural-number fuel bound strictly greater than the length of $A$ and every suffix $r$, decoding the encoding of $A$ followed by $r$ returns $(A,r)$.
hypotheses_covered: for each element of $A$, $f(g(a)\mathbin{++}r)=(a,r)$ for every suffix $r$
the length of $A$ is strictly less than the fuel bound
